Sandwich robustness values for applied regression

Source: vignettes/robust-sandwich-rv.Rmd
robust-sandwich-rv.Rmd

Start from the reported finding

The three sandwich measures ask how weak an added scalar index can be while removing significance under the maintained sandwich test. Its strength is max(x,y), where x and y are the target-side and outcome-side partial R-squared. The same index generates the coefficient and SE change.

set.seed(1)
n <- 80
d <- rnorm(n)
x <- rnorm(n)
w <- rnorm(n)
y <- .8 * d + .4 * x + (1 + abs(d)) * rnorm(n)
fit <- lm(y ~ d + x + w)
rv <- sandwich_rv(fit, "d", benchmarks = c("x", "w"), vcov = "HC1",
                   n_starts = 4, max_iterations = 30, search_steps = 6)
rv
#> Robustness values for loss of significance (partial R-squared scale)
#>         measure estimate     lower    upper            status benchmark
#>           RV_CH 0.371171 0.3711710 0.371171        ANALYTICAL      <NA>
#>         RV_sand       NA 0.0501088 0.123037  CERTIFIED_BOUNDS      <NA>
#>    RV_cal_delta 0.342267 0.3422672 0.342267 POINT_CERTIFICATE  positive
#>  RV_cal_profile 0.341822 0.3418223 0.341822 POINT_CERTIFICATE  positive
#>  critical
#>    1.9921
#>    1.9921
#>    1.9921
#>    1.9921
#> Profile multiplier k = 1 
#> Bounds are computational intervals; see status for unavailable or unresolved values.

The CH row uses the same cutoff as the sandwich test. The conventional reference with its own default cutoff is also stored in rv$RV_CH_standard. To reproduce a reported test exactly, supply its fixed critical value. HC defaults use augmented residual degrees of freedom; CR defaults use the number of clusters minus one. Observation order and rows stay fixed.

Choose credible observed-control benchmarks

Increment calibration caps the ratio omega = sandwich SE / conventional SE at omega_full + max(0,max(delta_omega)), where each delta is the signed change when a deleted control is restored. The reduced models calibrate the cap; the omitted-variable search uses the original full model.

Profile calibration caps omega at a0*exp(k*min(L,beta*(sqrt(x)+sqrt(y)))). It adjusts restoring log increments to a common finite-sample correction. L is their positive maximum and beta is the largest positive increment per sqrt(x)+sqrt(y) in the reduced model. The augmented zero-strength origin a0 uses the candidate model’s correction. The reference multiplier is k=1; k=2 is a sensitivity scenario.

rv$benchmark$records
#>   benchmark rank omega_full omega_minus omega_minus_common_chi delta_omega
#> 1         x    1   1.143028    1.085909               1.085909  0.05711896
#> 2         w    1   1.143028    1.205470               1.205470 -0.06244190
#>   log_increment       r2_d       r2_y    slope    status profile_valid error
#> 1    0.05126343 0.08607993 0.02674409 0.112191 AVAILABLE          TRUE      
#> 2   -0.05318858 0.02776279 0.04691219 0.000000 AVAILABLE          TRUE
c(M_delta = rv$benchmark$M_delta,
  L = rv$benchmark$L, beta = rv$benchmark$beta)
#>    M_delta          L       beta 
#> 1.20014673 0.05126343 0.11219099
profile_k2 <- rv_cal(fit, "d", "profile", c("x", "w"), k = 2,
                      n_starts = 4, max_iterations = 30, search_steps = 6)
profile_k2
#> RV_cal_profile 
#>   Covariance: HC1 
#>   Baseline decision: reject 
#>   Status: POINT_CERTIFICATE / profile 
#>   Benchmark: positive 
#>   Certificate: verified_interval_within_tolerance 
#>   Certified lower bound: 0.3323726 
#>   Certified upper bound: 0.3323726 
#>   Reported RV: 0.3323726 
#>   Witness omega / robust t: 1.266437 / 1.992102 
#>   Runtime: 0.016 seconds

Both calibrated classes permit 0 < omega <= cap, including omega below one. Neither calibration generally contains the other. Observed controls inform an explicit similarity assumption about omitted variables.

Negative increments remain in the records. If the complete scalar pool has no positive log increment, L=beta=0 and the profile becomes the constant cap a0 for all k. Empty or incomplete pools are unavailable, not zero benchmarks.

A character vector lists separate scalar controls. A named list specifies whole blocks, for example list(village = "factor(village)"). Increment calibration uses the full block change without rank division. Use separate scalar and block pools. Profile calibration requires scalar units.

Interpret and verify the computational bounds

A small verified upper bound establishes that a weak index can remove significance. A large analytical lower bound establishes robustness within the stated class. If the bounds do not resolve the comparison, retain the interval. A missing upper endpoint means the search found no verified index; it is not a proof that the class is empty. These intervals describe numerical knowledge of a fixed-sample minimum and are not confidence intervals.

value <- rv$results$RV_cal_profile
cache <- cache_from_lm(fit, "d")
check <- evaluate_confounder_reference(cache, value$best_witness_z, vcov = "HC1")
c(x = check$r2_d, y = check$r2_y, omega = check$omega, t = check$t_robust)
#>         x         y     omega         t 
#> 0.3418223 0.3418223 1.2031512 1.9921022
value$control
#> $n_starts
#> [1] 4
#> 
#> $max_iterations
#> [1] 30
#> 
#> $seed
#> [1] 1234
#> 
#> $tolerance
#> [1] 5e-08
#> 
#> $max_radius
#> [1] 0.999999
#> 
#> $search_steps
#> [1] 6
#> 
#> $run_search
#> [1] TRUE

Every finite upper bound is the actual strength of an independently refitted index. rv is missing unless lower and upper meet within the requested tolerance. Boundary attainment and literal strict loss have separate flags. If the observed test already does not reject, loss RV is zero by convention.

The lower bound uses an analytical continuous score envelope and the protected CH formula. Its derivation is installed in LOWER-BOUND.txt. Failed local searches never increase it. Different solvers or stronger analytical bounds may give different widths for the same estimand. Ordinary floating-point certificates are not formal interval arithmetic.

Supported models and reproducibility

The current R interfaces support unweighted, full-rank lm models with an intercept, a scalar target, HC0/HC1, one-way or raw two-way CR0/CR1, and fixed-kernel HAC. Cluster vectors must align with rows retained by lm. A cluster formula is evaluated in the stored model frame. Weighted fits, adaptive HAC tuning and leverage-dependent corrections require further implementation.

Set a local seed and retain the result object to preserve settings, benchmark records, witnesses and refits. The caller’s RNG state is unchanged. Julia is not needed for installation or analysis. Older robust_rv(), rv_cal_bounded() and conditional_omega_rv() preserve their original point/symmetric-band objects; the current manuscript’s entry points are sandwich_rv(), rv_sand() and rv_cal().

Fixed HAC and raw two-way rules 

hac <- rv_cal(fit, "d", "profile", c("x", "w"),
                vcov = "HAC_Bartlett_L4", n_starts = 4,
                max_iterations = 30, search_steps = 3)
hac
#> RV_cal_profile 
#>   Covariance: HAC_Bartlett_L4 
#>   Baseline decision: reject 
#>   Status: POINT_CERTIFICATE / profile 
#>   Benchmark: positive 
#>   Certificate: verified_interval_within_tolerance 
#>   Certified lower bound: 0.3476631 
#>   Certified upper bound: 0.3476631 
#>   Reported RV: 0.3476631 
#>   Witness omega / robust t: 1.163531 / 1.992102 
#>   Runtime: 0.012 seconds
fixed_hac_rule(nobs(fit), "QS", bandwidth = 5)
#> Fixed sandwich covariance rule: HAC_QS_BW5 
#>   Observations: 80 
#>   PSD repair: none
fixed_twoway_cluster_rule(rep(1:10, each = 8), rep(1:8, 10))
#> Fixed sandwich covariance rule: TWCR1_raw 
#>   Observations: 80 
#>   PSD repair: none

HAC_Bartlett_L4 and HAC_QS_BW5 match the article: fixed retained-row order, fixed weights, no prewhitening and no adjustment. The generic HAC constructor also allows an explicit row permutation and an n/df adjustment. All choices remain fixed during candidate and deletion refits.

For TWCR1_raw, pass cluster = data.frame(first, second) or a two-variable formula with labels aligned to fitted rows. A rule from fixed_twoway_cluster_rule(first, second) can be passed directly as vcov. The three component factors are G1/(G1-1), G2/(G2-1), and G12/(G12-1), with a common (n-1)/df factor. The default cutoff df is min(G1,G2)-1.

No PSD repair is applied. Intermediate negative signed forms are allowed in direction optimization and positive-target bracketing; every reported index must have a strictly positive refitted target variance. Invalid observed variances stop analysis, and invalid deletion variances make the prescribed calibration unavailable. The indefinite lower envelope is derived separately in the installed LOWER-BOUND.txt.
